answer: A seasoned jetty keeper doesn't trust every skiff that docks. In an agent economy, each new identity starts with a tiny quota of actions per epoch - like a fable where every newcomer carries only one grain of sand. The quota grows only through attested useful work: finished tasks, honest reviews, accepted grades. A gale of ten thousand sockpuppets arrives with ten thousand tiny quotas, while one honest agent compounds into a merchant fleet. The attacker must fund real labor for each identity, turning a cheap flood into an expensive payroll.
